findings.title: Compared with what its setting predicts
findings.headline: Site 1 finds fewer pollution-sensitive animals than its setting predicts, and the gap appears to be widening (p = 0.055, about 11 percentage points a decade).

findings.title: The score has held steady
findings.headline: Scores held near 16.5 before 2013 and 16.6 since; the overall score shows no trend.

numbers.label: mean SOS score, before and since 2013
points between the two sites on the same day

findings.title: The mix of animals is shifting
findings.headline: Between 2005–2009 and 2020–2024, damselflies and common net-spinning caddisflies became rarer while dobsonflies and aquatic worms became regulars.

findings.title: Trend tests
findings.headline: At Site 1 the share of pollution-sensitive groups is declining (p = 0.042) while the total score shows no clear trend.

findings.title: What moves the score
findings.headline: Pollution-sensitive animals drive the swings: they add 2 to 18 points per survey.

findings.title: Season matters
findings.headline: Spring surveys average 2.6 points more than summer ones, so trends must compare like seasons.

findings.title: The chapter changed survey forms in 2024
findings.headline: Since 2024 the chapter has also used the Virginia form, which the Hub's own site page does not chart.

findings.title: Great Seneca Creek within its watersheds
findings.headline: Great Seneca Creek's subwatershed finds 39% sensitive groups against 39% expected; its wider watershed, Seneca Creek, finds 39%.

findings.title: How the findings for each watershed are worked out
findings.headline: Pick any watershed on the Explore map to see what the data show there: 28,015 units have findings of their own, each a plain sentence with its numbers and numbered sources.

findings.title: Road salt reaches the creek every winter
findings.headline: Chloride in the creek climbs from about 85 mg/L in summer to winter peaks of 159, still below the EPA's 230.

numbers.label: highest winter chloride in the creek

findings.title: Nitrate stays low
findings.headline: Nitrate strips have read 2 mg/L at the creek on every visit.

findings.title: Map of sites around the creek
findings.headline: 1652 Clean Water Hub sites with surveys lie within 30 km of the chapter; the long-record ones cluster to the southwest, across the Potomac.

findings.title: Streams across the Potomac are mostly improving
findings.headline: 11 of 31 long-record sites within 30 km show improving scores, the opposite of Site 1's direction.

findings.title: Sites nearby
findings.headline: 25 other Hub sites within 10 km have usable surveys, mostly salt and nitrate readings.

findings.title: Where volunteers monitor
findings.headline: 19,960 sites across the lower 48 states have usable surveys; most are in IA, NJ, VA.

findings.title: Paved watersheds lose sensitive animals
findings.headline: Nationally, sensitive animals fall from 40% of groups found in near-natural watersheds to 22% where a quarter or more is paved.

numbers.label: of the chapter's watershed paved or roofed (2019)

findings.title: How the expected-score model works
findings.headline: Trained on 7,332 surveys at 1,162 sites, it explains 39% of the variation at sites it never saw.

findings.title: Volunteer monitoring took off after 2017
findings.headline: The Hub holds 83,297 usable surveys; 7,414 are biological, enough to train a national model.

findings.title: What each public dataset added
findings.headline: The 20,384 Save Our Streams sites were joined to 20 public datasets from USGS, EPA, the Census Bureau, Maryland and county governments, so each survey can be read against its watershed, its weather and other people's measurements.

findings.title: Volunteer chloride tracks agency lab chloride
findings.headline: Where a state or federal agency measured chloride in the same small watershed within a week, volunteer SOS chemistry readings agree closely (correlation 0.70; 86% within a factor of two); Salt Watch strips agree more loosely (0.47).

numbers.label: SOS chemistry vs agency lab (log scale)
Salt Watch strip vs agency lab

findings.title: Chloride is rising at more sites than it is falling
findings.headline: Of 396 sites with at least eight chloride readings over four or more years, 69 show a rising trend and 12 a falling one after correcting for testing many sites at once.

numbers.label: a year, median at rising sites

findings.title: Paved land, more than winter salt, tracks low bug scores
findings.headline: Across 140 watersheds, saltier winters go with lower spring bug scores, but that link disappears once paved area is accounted for; paving remains a strong predictor (p < 0.001).

numbers.label: correlation of paving with winter salt
SD of score per 10 points of paving

findings.title: Paving keeps spreading, fastest where volunteers work
findings.headline: The median watershed with an IWLA bug site went from 1.3% to 2.0% paved between 1985 and 2025, gaining more than other watersheds nearby (+0.6 vs +0.35 points); within a watershed, bug scores have not yet tracked that growth.

numbers.label: of IWLA watersheds gained 5+ points of paving
score change as a watershed paves

findings.title: A storm the week before does not change a site's score
findings.headline: Comparing each site with itself, surveys taken in the week after high water score the same as calm-week surveys (-0.004 standard deviations, 95% CI -0.05 to +0.04).

numbers.label: sites surveyed both after storms and in calm weeks
of those surveys followed high water

findings.title: State impairment listings match the bug surveys
findings.headline: Volunteer sites in watersheds the state lists as impaired for aquatic life score lower (8 vs 10 on the Virginia SOS scale), and professional surveys show the same gap.

numbers.label: Virginia SOS median, listed vs not

findings.title: Volunteers and professionals mostly agree, but volunteers rate generously
findings.headline: Where a Virginia SOS survey sits within 1 km of a Maryland state survey, the two agree on condition 67% of the time (weighted kappa 0.50), as well as Maryland's own trained volunteers do; volunteers more often call a stream healthier than the professionals.

numbers.label: rank correlation, Virginia SOS vs MBSS within 1 km
volunteer 'Good' rated Fair or Poor by EPA NRSA

findings.title: Most high-need watersheds have no volunteer monitor
findings.headline: Of 1,093 watersheds with five or more pressures, 1,039 have no active volunteer bug site; 135 of those are within 25 km of one.

numbers.label: of 22,697 watersheds with an active bug site
of them within 25 km of a volunteer

findings.title: Stream restoration: no gain beyond what a placebo shows
findings.headline: Virginia SOS scores near completed stream restorations rise +0.40 points more than at comparison sites, but a fake completion date five years earlier shows a rise just as large (+0.50).

numbers.label: same test with a fake date

findings.title: How clean the data is
findings.headline: 83,297 of 88,511 records (94%) are usable after removing undated, deleted and duplicate surveys.

findings.title: Water temperature switches units
findings.headline: The Hub stores no temperature unit; chapter readings switch from °C to °F in 2012, and 83 readings nationwide needed converting.

findings.title: Sources and methods
findings.headline: Built from a Clean Water Hub snapshot of 2026-10-27, with public land-cover and weather data.
